# **Intercept Live Design Phase: Team Brief**

Oct 20, 2026 · @Albert Santalo

## **About Intercept**

Intercept Telehealth provides 24/7 virtual critical care to hospitals and health systems, with board-certified intensivists covering ICU patients remotely across multiple facilities. Its leadership is turning Intercept from a tech-enabled services business into a Service-as-Software company, where its own technology, AI, and automation change the unit economics, reduce dependence on clinical staffing, and raise enterprise value. A capital raise is underway to fund that shift.

Archie Labs has already completed a strategy engagement with Intercept. It produced the investor narrative, a platform vision, an agentic AI opportunity map, an integration strategy for closed hospital systems, an initial set of high-fidelity screens, and the Intercept Live System Specification: eighteen modules across experience, intelligence, and operations layers, on shared Core Services and a governed set of AI agents. This phase builds directly on that work.

## **The project**

Between now and January 20, 2027, we turn the System Specification into a detailed design of Intercept Live's core clinical experience and a working prototype of it. Intercept will use both in its capital raise, grant applications, and hospital and customer discussions, so the prototype has to look and behave like the real product.

The scope is ten modules: the Provider Desktop, Tele-Critical Care Clinical Surveillance, Care Coordination, Clinical Documentation, Order Entry, Clinical Alerting, System and Client Administration, Virtual Sepsis, and Specialty Care Access, which adds on-demand specialist consults and the marketplace behind them.

We deliver three things: the module designs (user stories, screen designs, module definitions), the design system beneath them, and the interactive prototype, demonstrating about six scenarios agreed with Intercept. A handoff package in standard formats and a final readout to Intercept leadership close the phase.

We build the prototype in Archie as a full-stack application: a React frontend on an AWS-centric backend, fed by a real-time data simulator that streams synthetic data from in-room devices and hospital EHRs. Platform architecture, hospital integrations, and the production build are a later phase under a separate agreement. What we build here is their starting point, so the definitions and user stories matter as much as the screens.

## **In scope**

We design ten modules in detail, build the design system beneath them, and prove them in an interactive prototype. The Provider Desktop and the specialty care consult experience get the highest prototype fidelity; every other in-scope module is still fully designed.

**Modules (detailed design \+ prototype)**

* Experience layer: Provider Desktop (Single Pane of Glass), Tele-Critical Care Clinical Surveillance, Care Coordination, Communication & Telepresence, Clinical Documentation, Order Entry, Clinical Alerting & Events, System Administration, Client Administration  
* Intelligence layer: Virtual Sepsis  
* Specialty Care Access: on-demand specialist consults (tele-stroke, tele-cardiology, tele-psychiatry and adjacent specialties), specialist matching and the consult workflow, imaging review, structured recommendations back to the requesting hospital, and the marketplace infrastructure behind it. The System Specification only covers this at concept depth, so we write its specification as well as designing it.

**Design system.** Components, patterns, density model, and interaction standards, built so the production build can inherit and extend them across all eighteen modules.

**Prototype build.** A full-stack application built in Archie, with a React frontend and an AWS-centric backend, running on synthetic data.

**Real-time data simulator.** Internal Archie Labs tooling, not a deliverable to Intercept. It streams synthetic data into the prototype the way live hospital sources would: in-room devices (bedside monitors, ventilators, infusion pumps), lab and ADT feeds, and hospital EHRs. It drives the surveillance, alerting, and Virtual Sepsis scenarios, so it must produce realistic trends over time, such as a patient deteriorating, for those modules to react to. It runs only during demos, not continuously.

**Design tensions to resolve up front.** Information density without clutter, honest data provenance, visible AI activity, and graceful degradation when hospital data is thin or stale.

**Demonstration scenarios.** About six, identified jointly with Diego and the Intercept team early in the engagement. Each one must run end to end in the prototype. None are fixed yet.

**Starting inputs.** The Intercept Live System Specification and the high-fidelity screens from the strategy engagement.

## **Out of scope**

None of the following is done in this phase, even if Intercept asks for it informally. Route any such request to Carlos.

* **Deferred to the next phase:** Core Services substrate, backend and interface architecture, API design and data model, device and EMR integration, hospital integration specifications, the integration engine, the Hospital System Bridge, and the production build plan and estimate. The prototype has its own working backend, but the production platform architecture is designed in the next phase  
* **Deferred modules:** Protocol Framework, Clinical Analytics & Benchmarking, Compliance & Reporting, Provider Onboarding, Credentialing, Scheduling & Coverage, Hospital Onboarding & Deployment, Care Orchestration (5.10 to 5.17)  
* **No live connections:** the prototype does not connect to any hospital system or device; the real-time data simulator stands in for those feeds  
* **Not production software:** the prototype is a design and demonstration artifact, not for clinical use

## **Ground rules**

* **Synthetic data only.** No real patient information in the prototype, the data simulator, our working files, or screenshots.  
* **Show the sanctioned integration story.** The prototype will be shown to hospitals and investors. Do not depict screen-operated extraction or overlay fallback paths in anything Intercept may show externally.  
* **Patient data never crosses tenants.** No design should show patient data aggregated across hospital tenants.  
* **About six scenarios, then stop.** Scenarios beyond those agreed with Intercept go to Carlos as a change request.  
* **Build to the SOW descriptions.** Intercept must accept each deliverable in writing and has 10 business days to review it. They can reject only for specific nonconformance with what we committed to, so we deliver exactly that.  
* **Keep Archie internals out of the handoff.** Intercept can share the deliverables with third-party developers. Prompts, models, generation tooling, and the data simulator stay with us; the files they receive are standard formats any developer can use.  
* **Agree any external commitment with Albert first.** Dates, features, or scope promised to Intercept in working sessions go through Albert or Carlos.
